chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from al-Husayn ibn 'Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
The space between the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) and the heaven is [filled with] the angels descending and ascending.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the space between Imam Husayn's grave and the heavens?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) to emphasize the cosmic significance of Karbala, portraying the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) as a vertical axis connecting earth to heaven. This constant movement of angels underscores the Imam’s role as a spiritual conduit, reinforcing the Shia belief in the intercessory power and elevated ontological status of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. My father and all of my scholars narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ḥusain ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Abī ‘Uthmān, from Muḥammad ibn Fuďayl, from Isḥāq ibn ‘Ammār, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
The space between the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) and the heavens is (always) filled with angels who are descending and ascending (back and forth from the Ziyārah).
